introduction.text: The Basilica di San Pancrazio in Rome is a minor Catholic basilica that has served as a parish, conventual, and titular church since the 6th century. It is significant for its association with the martyr Saint Pancras, its long architectural evolution, and its role as a titular church for several popes.

history.description: Founded by Pope Symmachus in the 6th century, the basilica was built on the burial site of Saint Pancras.
Pope Gregory I transferred the church to the Benedictine Order after the Lombard sack of Montecassino.
Pope Honorius I enlarged the church in the 7th century to accommodate pilgrims and placed the saint's relics beneath the high altar.
In the 17th century the Discalced Carmelites remodeled the basilica.
The basilica was heavily damaged during the French attack on the Roman Republic in 1849 and was rebuilt in the 19th century.

design.description: The basilica retains a plain brick façade from the late 15th century, bearing the arms of Pope Innocent VIII.
The church was completely remodeled by the Discalced Carmelites in the 17th century, giving it its current layout.

art.description: The adjacent Museo di S. Pancrazio displays fragments of sculpture and pagan and early Christian inscriptions from the catacombs.
